topic: How air suspension (bagged cars) works the simple way

layout.title: How Air Suspension Works

shows.does: the car's steel springs shrink away and blue rubber air bags take their place
air sprays out of a bag and the car sinks down onto a big ball lying under it
a compressor appears, its fan spins, air runs down a hose and the car lifts off the ball
after a bump the car sinks and stays low while the small pump hums
an orange tank appears, fills with air and the bags refill fast
air rushes in, the bags swell and the car shoots up too high
a valve appears with a green light and the car settles to the right height
a glowing outline traces the bag
water drips from the valve onto the driveway
a glass water trap appears and fills with the caught water; the dripping stops
the car tips back, its rear end sinking under a heavy load
a row of valves appears, one per bag, and the car levels out
air sprays from the long lines under the car
white nylon lines appear clipped along the frame and the spray stops
the car sits low and scrapes over the ball with sparks, pushing it along
height sensors appear at each corner, blink, and the car lifts back up
the car rides up high and sways
the sensors blink and the car lowers and steadies
the car bounces up and down again and again
yellow shock absorbers appear beside the bags and the bouncing stops
the parked car slowly sinks as the bags leak down
a remote with a red button appears, its light glows and the car rises
the bags fill, the car lifts and the ball rolls out from under it
the finished bagged car with its kit

layout.why: A red car on a garage driveway, cut away low so its air bags show, with the air kit building up beside it in the order the air flows: compressor, tank, valve, water trap, a valve per bag, nylon lines, height sensors, shock absorbers and a remote. A big ball lies under the car: the leaking car sags onto it, the low car scrapes it, and the finished car lifts off it. Shots frame the car (and the kit when a kit part arrives), close on the bags.

sentences.text: If you swap steel springs for bags of air, you have air suspension.
But a bag leaks, and the car sags onto a ball.
So you add a compressor that pumps air back in.
But the slow pump lets the car sink after every bump.
So you add a tank that refills it in seconds.
But the tank's air rushes in, and the car shoots up.
So a valve lets air in or out.
This is an air spring.
But each time the valve opens, water drips out.
So a water trap catches it first.
But with water trapped, a heavy trunk tips it back.
So each bag gets its own valve to level it.
But now four valves need four long lines, and they leak.
So you clip tough nylon lines along the frame.
But low on its lines, the car scrapes the ball.
So height sensors at each corner lift it up.
But lifted high on the highway, the car sways.
So the sensors lower it as you speed up.
But lowered over a pothole, it bounces on and on.
So you add shock absorbers that stop the bouncing.
But parked overnight, slow leaks sink it while the shocks sit.
So a remote button pumps it back up.
Press the button, and your bags of air lift it off the ball.
Congratulations, you built a bagged car.

recurring.what: a big ball under the car: sagged on, scraped, and finally cleared
